US Orders Partial Diplomatic Departure From Saudi Arabia Amid Escalating Houthi Attacks

State Department Issues Ordered Departure

The United States State Department has ordered non-emergency government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia following a sharp escalation in regional conflict. The directive comes as cross-border strikes attributed to Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement have resulted in fatalities and targeted critical infrastructure.

According to official statements, the decision was prompted by increasing hostilities that present significant security risks. A State Department spokesperson noted that Houthi forces have increasingly engaged in attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure, leading to civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions.

Recent Casualties and Infrastructure Strikes

Recent attacks across Saudi Arabia have resulted in three reported deaths and multiple injuries. Saudi authorities confirmed that debris from a drone intercepted during an attempted attack on the Shaybah oil field, located near the border with the United Arab Emirates, killed two people. A separate strike at the King Fahd International Airport in Dammam resulted in one fatality and left eight individuals with injuries ranging from minor to serious.

These incidents follow a pattern of intensified missile and drone launches targeting Saudi airports, energy facilities, and military bases. Earlier this month, an attack struck the airport in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, marking one of the deadliest incidents in the kingdom in recent years.

Background and Conflict Escalation

The broader conflict stems from Yemen's civil war, which began in 2014 when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa, followed by a Saudi-led military coalition intervention in 2015. Although an informal ceasefire held for four years, hostilities unraveled in July after the Houthis declared a maritime embargo and resumed missile and drone operations.

The group stated its actions are in retaliation for a Saudi blockade and an airstrike on Sanaa airport. The Houthi maritime embargo in the Bab al-Mandab Strait has further impacted global shipping and contributed to rising oil prices, compounding supply route pressures already affected by closures in the Strait of Hormuz.

Practical Implications and Verification

For travelers and expatriates in the region, the State Department's ordered departure highlights a deteriorating security environment. The official advisory warns that hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly.

Readers can verify official travel advisories and updates directly through the US State Department or read the original reporting via the [BBC News report](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6x2vpk93770o).

Confirmed vs. Unknown Details

  • Confirmed: The US State Department ordered non-emergency personnel and families to leave Saudi Arabia; three people have been killed in recent strikes; attacks have targeted airports and oil infrastructure.
  • Unknown: Full tactical specifics of the recent airport strike remain undisclosed by officials, and investigations into specific weapon launches continue.
